items.headline: Intel shares drop 28% in a day on weak guidance despite 21% revenue growth
items.why: A stock that falls this hard on a growth quarter shows the market is pricing the outlook (a forecast ~20% drop in Q4 PC sales), not the results, so cyclical PC exposure is being repriced.

items.headline: AMD posts record $13.4B quarterly revenue, data-center sales near double at $8.5B, guides ~$17B for Q4
items.why: The guide eased worries that AI infrastructure spending is rolling over, while a 40% drop in gaming revenue shows the growth is concentrated in data centers.

items.headline: Reported US moves tighten chip export controls: advanced-chip exports to China halted, approvals withheld for a Chinese memory plant
items.why: Tighter export policy raises compute costs in China and adds supply-chain uncertainty for chipmakers with Chinese capacity (reported, not officially confirmed in the source).

items.headline: ASML lifts 2026 revenue forecast to EUR 44-45B; Kioxia reports record half-year profit on AI memory demand
items.why: Equipment and memory suppliers are still raising numbers, so the AI build-out is showing up in upstream orders even as device-chip names (handsets, PCs, Arm royalties) weaken.

items.headline: Spot bitcoin ETFs shed about $1.28B over Nov 2-6; bitcoin ends the week near $75.8K after a $74.9K low
items.why: Sustained ETF outflows removed a key source of steady demand, and the move down came with the broader chip and AI stock sell-off, showing crypto still trades with risk assets.

items.headline: Binance reopens withdrawals after the largest crypto theft on record (~$6.3B); users pull a net $3.6B in the first hours
items.why: The outflow was large but orderly, which is the test of whether a major exchange keeps customer trust after a breach; the investigation and recovery figures are still moving.

items.headline: US Treasury cuts exchange MEXC off from the US financial system; Russia to allow retail crypto purchases from Nov 17
items.why: Enforcement against offshore venues is tightening in the US while another large economy opens retail access, so regulatory divergence is widening.

items.headline: October US CPI rises 0.4% on the month, above the 0.3% expected; core up 0.3%
items.why: A hotter-than-expected print, after the Fed's first rate hike in three years in September, keeps the pressure on for another increase at the December meeting.

items.headline: Futures price a ~77% chance of a Fed hike on Dec 9, up from ~67% a week earlier, as October payrolls add 165K with unemployment at 4.1%
items.why: A labor market that is still adding jobs gives the Fed room to keep tightening, which is a headwind for rate-sensitive assets and long-duration equities.

items.headline: US-Iran peace hopes drag Brent down 16% in a week, its steepest weekly fall since the pandemic began, though ships are still being hit near the Strait of Hormuz
items.why: Oil is trading on diplomacy hopes rather than concrete progress, so the move can reverse quickly, and cheaper oil is what eased inflation fears across other markets this week.

sources.title: Oil and Iran (Reuters via Insurance Journal)

items.headline: Gold rebounds to ~$4,100/oz, up more than $250 from its Oct 30 one-year low of $3,869.85
items.why: A weaker dollar, lower Treasury yields and falling oil outweighed rate-hike risk, showing gold is trading on real yields and the dollar more than on headline risk.

items.headline: Brent settles near $97.57 and WTI near $90.45 after the sharpest weekly drop since 2020
items.why: Oil is still near $100 despite the slide, and a JPMorgan estimate of a 1.4M barrel-per-day surplus in October is the case for lower prices if Middle East flows keep recovering.

sources.title: Oil and Iran (Reuters via Insurance Journal)

items.headline: Silver flat near $52.23, platinum up 1.6% to $1,520.75, palladium up 3.8% to $1,042.24 on Nov 5; Poland's central bank reaches its 700-tonne gold target
items.why: Industrial and precious metals rose together on the weaker dollar, while continued official-sector buying remains a floor under the gold bid.

items.headline: Nasdaq-100 ETF (QQQ) recovers from a break below support; a daily close above $700 is the level to confirm it
items.why: Until that close happens, the bounce is a recovery inside a damaged structure, and a rejection at $700 would show buyers still have work to do.

items.headline: Semiconductor ETF (SMH) tests a support cluster (declining trend line, weekly 50-period average, July low) with resistance near $540
items.why: Several independent levels stacked in one zone make it the line the chip trade has to hold; a decisive break would weaken the bullish setup.

items.headline: Bitcoin fails to close above $80,559 resistance; this week's range ran from $74,921 to $81,004; US crude holds $86.90 support
items.why: Bitcoin was rejected at a known resistance and sits in the lower half of its range, while crude's $86.90 level is the line that decides whether oil's selling is exhausted.
